solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cleric upset a group of people

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of cleric are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman has annoyed some of his congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like what the cleric did to the group, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a set of people sharing an interest, as in a circle of friends.

clue.text: Pot or tin basin broken

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of basin are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pot, a tin or a basin got broken in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a kitchen container to match the tin and basin, but it is slang for the drug; 'or' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is a slang term for the drug made from the hemp plant.

clue.text: They have their teeth on edge

definitions.text: They have their teeth on edge

parts.words: They have their teeth on edge
parts.note: read literally, these are mechanisms whose toothed wheels have teeth around the rim, not people who are nervous

explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel or bar, the teeth set around its edge and engaged by a pawl.

clue.text: Crazy, perhaps, but often with motive

definitions.meaning: slang for mad, from the Spanish word
this word, followed by the word motive, makes the name for a railway engine

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a play: the answer added to MOTIVE gives LOCOMOTIVE, and the answer is also the short form for a train engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is informal slang for mad, and the clipped form of a railway engine.

clue.text: What scores of young people are in?

definitions.text: What scores of young people are in?

parts.words: What scores of young people are in?
parts.note: a score is twenty, so several scores read as a decade of age in which young adults find themselves

explanation.definitionFit: The decade of life from age twenty to twenty-nine, when someone is a young adult.

clue.text: Man going to the match who couldn't stop the salt pouring out

definitions.text: Man going to the match who couldn't stop the salt pouring out

parts.words: Man going to the match who couldn't stop the salt pouring out
parts.note: the match is a marriage, and the salt is an old sailor who told his long tale to a listener unable to leave

explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, an old sailor (an 'old salt') stops a man on his way to a marriage feast and makes him hear the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The listener in Coleridge's poem is a guest heading to a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: He floated a company to avoid liquidation

definitions.text: He floated a company to avoid liquidation

parts.words: He floated a company to avoid liquidation
parts.note: reads as a businessman launching a firm, but describes the Bible's ark builder keeping his family and animals afloat to escape the flood

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark and floated it with his household and animals to survive the flood.

clue.text: Peruvians head East as a precaution

indicators.note: head means go in front of, so the Peruvians come before the compass point in this down entry

parts.note: the Incas were the native people of ancient Peru

explanation.surface: Travellers from Peru make for the east just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a safeguard against something happening, a synonym of precautionary.

clue.text: Painstaking people enjoy this activity

parts.note: painstaking read as pain-taking: people who take pleasure in inflicting pain

explanation.definitionFit: This is the practice of deriving pleasure from inflicting pain on others.

clue.text: Mark breaks into church

indicators.note: breaks means smashes apart, so the letters of the word into are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone with a grudge forces their way into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks into' looks like a burglary; in fact 'breaks' shuffles INTO into NOTI, followed by CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to take notice of it, to observe it.

clue.text: Lent is brought forward

definitions.meaning: lent as in a loan of money given in advance
moved on or put earlier in time

explanation.surface: The Christian fast falls earlier this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the season before Easter, but it is the past tense of lend: money advanced is money lent.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, and an advanced date is one brought forward.

clue.text: Relative finds Ned conscious after smash

indicators.note: a smash is a crash that breaks things up, so the letters of Ned and conscious are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family member finds Ned has come round after a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after smash' suggests a road accident with someone regaining consciousness; 'smash' is the anagram signal and 'after' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of a parent's first cousin is a family member at this more distant degree of kinship.

clue.text: Current male desire

parts.note: AC is alternating current
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man's present longing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it intensely.

clue.text: Son in row sent back for further examination

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the combined letters are read in the reverse direction
in places the son inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A son caught up in a row is sent home to sit a further test.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside TIER to give TISER, which 'sent back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after failing, a second examination.

clue.text: Is first and last a course at Oxford

indicators.note: first and last means the word is placed both at the start and at the end, so it appears twice

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is the first and final course of study at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a degree programme, but it is a watercourse: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The river Thames is called by this name where it passes through Oxford, a watercourse there.

clue.text: Note reciprocation about a point of principle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the paired notes go around the point

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: reciprocation is a returning in kind, so the note is given back in reverse

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A musical note returns the favour about a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: TE followed by its reversal ET gives TEET, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a principle.

clue.text: Gain favour with a hot dish

definitions.meaning: to ... favour is to seek approval by flattery
a spicy dish from South Asian cooking

explanation.surface: A chef wins approval with a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb appears in the idiom 'curry favour', and the noun is a spiced dish.

clue.text: Where a marathon man eventually makes his name?

definitions.text: Where a marathon man eventually makes his name?

parts.words: Where a marathon man eventually makes his name?
parts.note: a marathon is a long race, so a runner wins fame in that distance; the phrase also means ultimately

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means over a long period, ultimately, while literally describing a long-distance race.

clue.text: In divorce town five had a meal together to patch things up

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces
V is the Roman numeral for five
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Five people in Reno dine together to settle their differences.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate is to repair and restore, to patch something up.

clue.text: Embraces sweetheart and wives

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter
wives are spouses

explanation.surface: A man hugs his girlfriend and his wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but means the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to embrace or adopt it.

clue.text: The rear squad ordered to base

indicators.note: ordered means arranged or commanded, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The squad at the back is commanded to return to base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a military command but rearranges THE REAR SQUAD; 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is the main base or centre of operations of an organisation.

clue.text: Chest is tender after cold

indicators.note: after places the tender below the cold in this down entry

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: Someone's chest is sore after a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like sore, but it is the verb offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for valuables.

clue.text: A bit of a nut, the officer, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: The officer is said to be slightly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nut' looks like slightly crazy, describing the officer, but it is the edible part inside a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel is the inner part of a nut, a piece of it.

clue.text: Finished and left

explanation.surface: It's done and someone has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended, and also remaining, as in food left over.

clue.text: Police chase ends in the wood

parts.note: cops are police officers

indicators.note: ends means the last letter of chase is taken

explanation.surface: Officers pursue a suspect who ends up hiding among trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood or thicket.

clue.text: Prepare and serve a bird, none now left

parts.note: to do food is to prepare it
to do time is to serve a sentence

explanation.surface: Cook and serve up a bird though there are none left.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct flightless bird, none surviving.

clue.text: East European not quite in bondage

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a slave is someone held in bondage

explanation.surface: An Eastern European almost enslaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav is a member of the peoples of Eastern Europe speaking Slavic languages.

clue.text: Villain putting squeeze on the leader

indicators.note: on places the squeeze beneath the leading letter in this down entry
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hug is a squeeze

explanation.surface: A criminal leans on the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting the squeeze on' looks like pressuring someone, but it puts HUG after T, the leader of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent criminal, a villain.

clue.text: The ultimate competitor

parts.note: reads as the best athlete of all, but means one competing in the last round

explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who reaches the last match of a contest, its deciding round.

clue.text: Cuts and shares out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of shares are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a cake and hands out pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to cut, as with wool or metal.

clue.text: Appropriate, regarding the eastern Mediterranean

parts.note: re means about or regarding
the Levant is the region of the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A fitting remark about the eastern Mediterranean region.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or appropriate to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Consents, but will be a long time coming round again

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the long time encloses the word for again

parts.note: ages means a long time
re is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, but it will take forever for them to come round to it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' looks like changing one's mind, but it signals one piece surrounding another; 'but will be' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to something is to consent to it.
